The SHARE Act is a step in the right direction—rural healthcare shortages are a direct result of bureaucratic overreach strangling medical professionals with redundant licensing hurdles. While streamlining licensure helps, the real issue is systemic: Washington’s addiction to red tape extends far beyond healthcare. 

Look at the Investment Accelerator, which fast-tracks billion-dollar projects by slashing permitting delays. If we can expedite ports and tech hubs, why does it take years for a nurse’s license to cross state lines? The answer? Bloated agencies protecting their turf instead of patients. 

Cut the paperwork, empower states, and watch rural communities thrive without D.C.’s “help.”

Congressman Mann’s bill highlights a critical truth: taxpayer-funded programs must prioritize Americans in genuine need—veterans, seniors, disabled citizens—not subsidize bureaucratic bloat or misuse. Every dollar diverted to ineligible recipients is stolen from those relying on SNAP and Medicaid as lifelines.

The Fair Tax Act’s focus on gutting IRS overreach aligns with redirecting resources to real solutions: tackling veteran homelessness, drug addiction, and mental health crises. Washington’s addiction to expanding handouts without accountability fuels dependency.

Trim the waste, protect the vulnerable, enforce eligibility—no more blank checks for D.C.’s inefficiency.

The PBM Reform Act is a start, but let’s not pretend it’s a cure-all. PBMs like CVS Caremark and OptumRx have been fleecing taxpayers for years—marking up generics 1000%, steering patients to their own pharmacies, and pocketing billions through spread pricing. The FTC exposed their scams, yet this bill still lets them operate as middlemen.

Banning spread pricing in Medicaid? Good. Delinking PBM pay from drug costs? Better. But real reform means dismantling the entire racket, not just trimming its claws.

Until Congress guts PBMs’ monopoly power, Big Pharma’s D.C. puppets will keep rigging the system.

Congressional oversight and public scrutiny are overdue—see the full breakdown: https://t.co/x7W11GQUjX
